nodes.plm_caption: This video shows a person removing the ceiling light of a car. A car can be seen in the background. The person removes the ceiling light and works on it inside the car. summary.brief: A person replaces the vehicle’s ceiling dome lights with RECON LED bulbs, showing removal, installation, testing, and ending with RECON branding screens.
summary.detailed: The video begins with a series of RECON branding slides and an introductory title. A man wearing a black T‑shirt sits in the back seat of a truck and pulls out a small flat‑head screwdriver. He uses the screwdriver to pry the trim pieces of the rear ceiling dome light, exposing the incandescent bulb. He removes the hot bulb with the tool to avoid burns, then squeezes the tabs of a new LED bulb for a snug fit and inserts the LED into the recessed housing, angling it toward the driver and passenger. He slides the trim back into the headliner and ensures it sits flat. He repeats the same procedure on the front dome light, prying its trim, removing the old bulb, fitting a new LED bulb, adjusting its orientation, and reseating the trim. After both lights are fitted, he turns on the vehicle’s map lights to verify that the new LEDs illuminate correctly. The segment concludes with a view of the installed lights followed by black screens displaying the RECON logo and website address.

action.detailed: Use a flat‑head screwdriver to pry out each ceiling light trim, remove the hot incandescent bulb, squeeze the tabs of the new LED bulb, insert it into the housing, angle it toward the driver and passenger, reseat the trim, and test the illumination.

summary.brief: A man installs a RECON LED dome light in a vehicle using a small flat‑head screwdriver.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a series of RECON branding slides that introduce the LED dome‑light installation guide. After the title cards, a man wearing a black T‑shirt leans into the back seat of a Silverado and begins the retrofit. He first inserts a small flat‑head screwdriver into the retention tabs of the original dome‑light housing and pries the unit out of the headliner, pulling the hot bulb free while keeping his hands protected. He then squeezes the tabs on a new LED bulb, plugs the bulb into the wiring, and angles it toward the driver and passenger as desired. The housing is slid back into the ceiling opening so it sits flat, and the original screws are re‑installed with the screwdriver. He tests the new light by turning it on and off, confirms the fit, and then replaces the cover, completing the installation.

action.detailed: Use a small flat‑head screwdriver to pry out the old dome‑light housing, remove the hot bulb, squeeze the tabs on the new LED bulb and plug it in, position and angle the bulb as desired, slide the housing back into the headliner, secure it with the original screws, and test the light by turning it on and off.
